standards.name: Article Minimum Information Standard (AMIS)
standards.abstract: AMIS (Article Minimum Information Standard) is a checklist-style guideline developed and maintained by the Aniseed team to improve the reporting of experiments on ascidian (Ciona) development and gene expression so that published articles contain the minimal metadata needed for curation into the Aniseed database. It applies to experiments that produce spatial-temporal expression patterns (in situ hybridization, immunohistochemistry), molecular and anatomical perturbations, and resulting molecular or morphological phenotypes. The standard lists mandatory and additional useful items to report (e.g. developmental stage, clone/probe identity, perturbation tool and timing, wild-type controls, and use of the Aniseed anatomical ontology) and explicitly extends the MISFISHIE minimal-information concepts for these experiment types.

classification.rationale: The source presents prose guidance and a checklist of mandatory/useful items to report for different experiment types rather than a field-level table or an ordered workflow. Each listed line is an instruction to authors (what to report), so the material is best represented as a set of principles.

principles.principle: Developmental stage at which the expression was determined, according to the table of Hotta et al. (2007)
principles.evidence: Developmental stage at which the expression was determined, according to the table of Hotta et al. (2007)

principles.principle: Clone(s) used to synthesize the in situ hybridization probes used in the experiment, transgenic construct in the case of electroporations, or antibody, with reference, used in immunohistochemistry.
principles.evidence: Clone(s) used to synthesize the in situ hybridization probes used in the experiment,  transgenic construct in the case of electroporations, or antibody, with reference, used in immunohistochemistry.

principles.principle: Annotation: use the anatomical ontology of Aniseed to describe the territories of expression in legends and main text.
principles.evidence: Annotation: use the anatomical ontology of Aniseed to describe the territories of expression in legends and main text.

principles.principle: (Additional useful) Picture, comments in figure legend.
Identity of the deregulated molecule: indicate the corresponding gene/transcript model deregulated, preferring KH (Satou et al., 2008) models, followed by JGI v1.0 and ENSEMBL models.
principles.evidence: Identity of the deregulated molecule: The biological name of the gene can be ambiguous. It is preferable to indicate the corresponding gene/transcript model deregulated with a preference for KH (Satou et al., 2008) models, followed by JGI v1.0 and ENSEMBL models.

principles.principle: Type of interference with gene function: specify gain-of-function or loss-of-function.
principles.evidence: Type of interference with gene function: gain-of-function or loss-of-function.

principles.principle: Molecular tool used to deregulate the gene, with either reference of a previous study using this tool, or the precise sequence (MOs, mRNAs) or origin (Small molecules) of the tool.
principles.evidence: Molecular tool used to deregulate the gene, with either reference of a previous study using this tool (eg FGF9/16/20 MO described in Imai et al., 200XX), or the precise sequence (MOs, mRNAs) or origin (Small molecules) of the tool.

principles.principle: Stage of onset of the perturbation (e.g. time of injection for morpholinos).
principles.evidence: Stage of onset of the perturbation (eg. time of injection for morpholinos).

principles.principle: Time of perturbation: report Hotta stage when the structure(s) was/were removed or when the explants(s) was/were isolated.
principles.evidence: Time of perturbation: Hotta stage when the structure(s) was/were removed or when the explants(s) was/were isolated.

principles.principle: Removed anatomy part or explant: use the Aniseed anatomical dictionary to describe the removed anatomy part(s) or the type of explant isolated.
principles.evidence: Removed anatomy part or explant: use the Aniseed anatomical dictionary to describe the removed anatomy part(s) or the type of explant isolated.

principles.principle: Description of the molecular or anatomical perturbation leading to the phenotype.
principles.evidence: Description of the molecular or anatomical perturbation leading to the phenotype.

principles.principle: Developmental stage at which the expression of the target gene was determined, according to the developmental table of Hotta et al. (2007).
principles.evidence: Developmental stage at which the expression of the target gene was determined, according to the developmental table of Hotta et al. ( 2007)

principles.principle: Clone(s) used to synthesize the in situ hybridization probes used in the experiment, transgenic construct in the case of electroporations, or antibody, with reference, used in immunohistochemistry. (for molecular phenotype assessment)
principles.evidence: Clone(s) used to synthesize the in situ hybridization probes used in the experiment, transgenic construct in the case of electroporations, or antibody, with reference, used in immunohistochemistry.

principles.principle: Wild-type control: clearly indicate the expression profile of the wild type control determined in the same ISH or immunocytochemistry experiment as the experimental sample.
principles.evidence: Wild-type control: Clearly indicate the expression profile of the wild type control determined in the same ISH or immunocytochemistry experiment as the experimental sample.

principles.principle: Annotation: use the anatomical ontology of Aniseed to describe the territories in which the expression pattern of the target gene differs between wild-type control and experimental sample.
principles.evidence: Annotation: use the anatomical ontology of Aniseed to describe the territories in which the expression pattern of the target gene differs between wild-type control and experimental sample.

principles.principle: (Additional useful) Pictures of embryos with affected and wild-type expression patterns, comments in figure legend.
principles.evidence: Pictures of embryos with affected and wild-type expression patterns, comments in figure legend.

principles.principle: For morphological phenotypes: description of the molecular or anatomical perturbation.
principles.evidence: Description of the molecular or anatomical perturbation

standards.notes: Source: Aniseed 'AMIS, The Article Minimum Information Standard' page. The material is a collection of minimal-reporting checklists for several experiment types (wild-type expression, molecular perturbation, anatomical perturbation, molecular phenotype, morphological phenotype) and explicitly references MISFISHIE and the Hotta et al. developmental table as standards to follow.

standards.name: ANISEED Anatomical Ontology (Anatomical dictionary)
standards.abstract: ANISEED's anatomical ontology describes anatomical territories and cells across developmental stages of ascidian embryos (e.g., Ciona spp. and other tunicates). The resource integrates ontological terms (OBO format) with lineage, fate and biometry information and links those anatomical terms to expression and phenotype data. ANISEED is the implementation of the NISEED system for ascidians and is maintained as part of the ANISEED database and web portal; it is presented in Tassy et al., Genome Research (2010) and distributed via the ANISEED site (downloads include an OBO-formatted 'Anatomical territories - Developmental stages' file). The ontology is used to trace progenitor/progeny relationships (lineage), to query expression patterns by fate or territory, and to provide quantitative biometry (volume/shape/contact) for reconstructed embryos.

classification.rationale: The source material presents the anatomical dictionary as an ontology / graph (an OBO file and online interfaces that expose lineage, progenitor/progeny relationships, and links between structures). The content describes nodes (territories/cells/terms) and explicit relationships (lineage, progeny, neighbours), i.e. a directed acyclic graph, rather than a flat checklist of named data fields or purely prescriptive principles.

anatomical_territory.name: Anatomical territory (ontology term)
anatomical_territory.description: A named anatomical structure or territory defined in the ANISEED anatomical ontology, covering cells and higher-order structures across developmental stages.
anatomical_territory.evidence: Upon selection of a structure: The "In situ data" button will give access to all genes expressed in this structure, The "lineage" button will show you all progenitors and progeny (the interface will improve soon), The "biometry" button only works with cells, and gives access to the volume, surface, shape, and neighbours of the selected cell with a quantitation of the surface of contacts (only for 16- and 32-cell stages so far).

lineage.name: Lineage (progenitor/progeny relationships)
lineage.description: Lineage information linking anatomical territories across stages (progenitors and progeny), allowing tracing of developmental ancestry and descendant relationships.
lineage.evidence: You can now trace the lineage of a structure and use this to query for genes expressed in a precise lineage across developmental stages.

fate.name: Fate (final fates of blastomeres/structures)
fate.description: Annotations describing the final fates that given blastomeres or structures will adopt (used for fate-based searches across precursor territories).
fate.evidence: In search by fate mode, the user specifies a list of fates at the hatching larva (stage 26) and retrieves expression patterns in any precursor territory that gives rise these fates.

biometry.name: Biometry / Morphometrics
biometry.description: Quantitative geometrical descriptors for cells in reconstructed 3D embryos (volume, surface, shape descriptors, contact surface areas), currently available for selected stages.
biometry.evidence: Thanks to the 3D data we obtained and quantified using the 3D embryo Handler software and 3D embryo reconstructions, we provide some informations relative to neighbourhood relationships, shape of blastomeres, etc.... This is currently only available for two stages of Ciona embryos: 16- and 32-cell, but we are now building up a collection of reconstructed embryos and their biometrical analysis will gradually be put online.

neighbours.name: Neighbours / contact relationships
neighbours.description: Information and queries about neighbouring cells and contact surfaces between cells (used to retrieve cells within a distance or with particular contact areas).
neighbours.evidence: Neighbours interface: Select your favorite cells within the anatomical dictionary (beware this only works with cells, not higher order structures), a maximal( or minimal) distance for cells of interest, a minimal or maximal surface of contact and the system will retrieve a list of relevant cells.

in_situ_data.name: In situ / expression data linked to territory
in_situ_data.description: Expression data (in situ hybridization, reporter assays, immunolocalization) linked to anatomical territories and retrievable from the anatomical dictionary.
in_situ_data.evidence: Upon selection of a structure: The "In situ data" button will give access to all genes expressed in this structure, The "lineage" button will show you all progenitors and progeny (the interface will improve soon), The "biometry" button only works with cells, and gives access to the volume, surface, shape, and neighbours of the selected cell with a quantitation of the surface of contacts (only for 16- and 32-cell stages so far).

ontology_file.name: OBO-formatted anatomy ontology (download)
ontology_file.description: The downloadable ontology file representing anatomical territories by developmental stage (OBO format) provided in the ANISEED downloads.

territories_search_mode.name: Search by territories mode
territories_search_mode.description: Search interface mode where users specify a list of territories within a time window to retrieve expression patterns in those territories.
territories_search_mode.evidence: In search by territories mode, the user specifies a list of list of territories existing within the time window considered, and retrieves expression patterns in these precise territories.

standards.notes: Nodes and edges reflect the ontology/graph structure and the ANISEED web interfaces described in the source material (OBO file, lineage tracing, fate and territory searches, biometry and neighbours modules). Evidence quotes are verbatim excerpts from the provided ANISEED pages and release notes.
